title: Directed colimits of injectives are derived-section acyclic on compact opens
statement: Let X have a basis of compact opens and compact pairwise intersections of compact opens. Let I be a nonempty directed preorder and J a diagram of injective abelian sheaves on the open site of X. For every compact open U and every n >= 0, R^{n+1} Gamma(U,-) applied to colim J is zero. Derived sections are as in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. The diagram is over I itself, not Discrete I.

source.place: Lemma 01FF, final acyclicity claim and its proof using Lemma 01EW

proof.text: Take B to be the compact opens and Cov the finite coverings by compact opens. Every cover of a member of B has such a refinement by the basis and compactness. Every nonempty finite intersection of the covering opens is compact by induction using the intersection hypothesis. Empty covers occur only over the empty open.

Sections on each intersection commute with the directed colimit. Each Cech term is a finite product of these sections. Finite products of abelian groups commute with filtered colimits, so the Cech complex of colim J is the termwise colimit of the Cech complexes of J_i.

Each injective J_i has zero positive Cech cohomology. Exact filtered colimits of abelian groups commute with homology, so colim J is Cech-acyclic for all covers in Cov. Use the site injective Cech theorem only with the coefficient and Ext universes equal.

The site Cech vanishing criterion applied to B and Cov gives zero positive object cohomology over every compact open. The natural comparison of object cohomology with derived sections gives the stated vanishing. The empty open has zero sections; the empty Cech products are zero groups.
